main_text.head:
4. MATERIAM parti inflammatæ affi xam vacuantibus, vt dicta phlebotome ad coloris sanguinis mutationē, vt medicamento purgante, si materia ad ventrem repat: purgante autem non valenter, nec astringendo, sed tantùm leniendo. Vitanda igitur scam moniata, licet Gal. lib. 2. rat. victus acutorum, hieram quæ colocynthidem recipit, propinet, & Hipp. ibidem elleborum, & peplium valentia medicamenta, quòd illorum ætate clementia nondum erant inuenta, qualia sunt cassia, ad sescunciam cum decocto thoracico sumpta. Vitandæ etiam myrobalani citreæ, licet sint cholagogæ: quia immoderatius astringunt. Eadem ratione rhabarbarum hic damnat Arcul. rhabarbari tamen drachmæ duæ vel tres, cū pauca spica minutim concisa infusæ, aut potius nostro more sine spica, horis decem vel duodecim in aqua violarū, &

page.notes: The last line of the page reads "horis decem vel duodecim in aqua violarū," followed by a ligature mark "&" at the right; the marginal ornament is a printer's flourish, not text. Some words are doubtful in the cursive italic (e.g. "astringendo", "cholagogæ"); transcribed as read. The paragraph following the head is a continuation of the sentence, so the head is set in the middle of the text as a section heading.
